text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Popular television presenter Yevgeny Kiselyov has filed a libel suit against President Yeltsin's former bodyguard Alexander Korzhakov.
- Dozens of tonnes of British beef, illegally imported into Russia, have been consumed.
- Russian Unikombank commercial bank is working to dispel a scandal stirred up by the Central Bank.
- Value added tax accounts for over half of the Russian state budget and the tax service would like to push the figure even higher.

- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, former head of the gas monopoly, told fresh-faced reformers in the government to double-check their calculations before starting experimenting with natural monopolies.
- Belarus government is planning to further tighten control over commercial banks.
- Russia's Aeroflot flag carrier is to pursue its promotional rock bottom fare schemes to lure more foreign customers to its international fligts.
- A number of top managers have left the Rosneft oil company.

- Alfa-bank is pursuing an arbitration court action against the West Siberian metallurgical plant in an attempt to get a bank representative appointed to head the outside management at the financially crippled company.
- A string of trading companies belonging to Russia's defence ministry have been earmarked for privatisation.
- Philip Morris tobacco company is to shake up its distribution network in Russia.
SEVODNYA
- Unikombank president Nina Galanicheva says the Central Bank gave her company a clean bill of health.
- The Mir space station plunged into darkness on Thursday after a cosmonaut on board mistakenly unplugged the wrong cable.
- Duma experts continue discussion of the draft tax code.
- The Tax Service wants the new tax code to be written in a form understandable to every Russian.
- The date for privatisation of defence ministry trading companies will be set after August 1.
- Independent gas producers have received access to Russia's gas pipelines.
- Russian natural monopolies may be a tough nut to crack for those reformers who want to use them as guinea pigs in their economic experiments.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The latest decrees by President Yeltsin supposed to overhaul the Russian armed forces fall short of a comprehensive concept of army reform, says former defence minister Igor Rodionov.
- Russian space station Mir on Thursday once again flew out of position in space after a cosmonaut on board disconnected the wrong cable.
- The draft tax code is likely to be dramatically transformed during debate in the Duma.
- Government regulation of natural monopolies has already given some positive results, says the economics ministry.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
